key_insight: VULCAN combines gradient-free ansatz growth, circuit compression, and perturbative correction to lower the quantum measurement cost of chemically accurate electronic-structure calculations.
engineering_relevance: Smaller operator pools, controlled circuit depth, and reduced qubit requirements offer a resource-efficient route toward quantum chemistry on quantum computers.
method: Grow full ansatz layers using Variational Double Bracket Flow and a linearly scaling operator pool, eliminating Hamiltonian-gradient measurements for operator selection.
Compress circuits through state-overlap measurements and reduce qubit requirements via dominant-determinant subspace projection.
Apply GPU-accelerated stochastic Epstein–Nesbet perturbation theory (ENPT2) to enable early termination at chemical accuracy.
evidence_signal: Emulations up to 32 logical qubits report chemical accuracy at 5–20% of batched ADAPT-VQE's measurement cost for hydrogen chains, BeH2, and H2O; one VULCAN layer plus ENPT2 also reaches chemical accuracy for 32-qubit C3H6, where the baseline does not.
watch_item: Results rely on high-performance emulation; robustness to hardware noise and the total cost of compression and classical ENPT2 post-processing remain implementation concerns.
paper_title: Grow, Compress, and Perturb: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Pathway to Scalable Quantum Chemistry on Quantum Computers
